_comment: Hand-written fixture for tests/models-check.mjs. Nothing in it was captured from the live
provider at test time: models-check used to fetch https://rustvy.xyz/v1/models and
https://rustvy.xyz/models on every run, which made the suite's outcome a fact about the
network rather than about the code. host-wiring saw it time out at 21.8 s and lead saw it
pass forty minutes later with nothing in the repository changed between.
This file is separate from model-sync.json on purpose. That fixture's island and wire
halves DISAGREE by design — it holds a zonal twin and a catalogue-only sentinel to prove
the plan retires and re-adds correctly. models-check asserts the opposite property, that
the two sources agree, so it needs a fixture built for agreement and one built for
disagreement. Reusing model-sync.json would have made the agreement assertion false on
arrival and somebody would have weakened it to get green.
The live path survives as an opt-in mode, because it covers something a fixture cannot:
that the real provider's two answers still parse and still agree.
$env:DSH_RUSTVY_LIVE_MODELS_CHECK = '1'; node tests/models-check.mjs
Every id is named in _roles. An id with no role is decoration and proves nothing.

_roles.claude-opus-5-5: full record: a display name that differs from the id, a vendor, both modalities and four reasoning levels. Proves a hand-written description survives regeneration rather than being rebuilt from the catalogue
_roles.glm-5.3: the only record whose output cap is 8192 rather than 128000, so a capacity actually read from the catalogue is distinguishable from a default that happens to match
_roles.gpt-6.1-sol: an ordinary enabled record, present in both halves
_roles.ahmia-v7-pro: an ordinary enabled record, present in both halves; models-check has always printed this id, so keeping it means the generated output is still comparable to earlier runs
_roles.kimi-k3: only two reasoning levels, so a model that does not offer the full ladder is exercised. It is also the id the disagreeing half drops, which is what makes that half disagree
_roles.no-capacity-model: no contextK and no maxOutputTokens: the plan must say the window is unpublished rather than inventing one, and the schema check must accept an entry with neither field
_roles.retired-model: enabled: false. Excluded from the island fallback and absent from the wire, so the two halves still agree — the property under test is agreement, not inclusion
_roles.abyss/qwen3.8-max: zone: abyss. A zonal record is not standard-zone membership, so the fallback excludes it and the wire does not serve it. Its presence is what proves the fallback filters on zone rather than on enabled alone
_roles.phantom-model: appears ONLY in the disagreeing wire half. If it reaches the generated entries in agreeing mode, the suite read the wrong half of this file

_comment: The same island with a wire answer that does not match it: kimi-k3 is missing and a
phantom id is present. The suite asserts that this half does NOT agree, which is what
makes the agreement assertion mean something — a check that cannot fail is not a check.
This is the shape the live provider produced on 2026-11-02, when it dropped five models
in the morning and re-enabled them in the afternoon.
